before_times: What heats or cools the home: a gas furnace, a boiler, a heat pump, oil, central AC or a mini-split
What's happening: no heat, no cooling, a noise, water around the unit, or it keeps turning on and off
Is a carbon monoxide alarm going off, or is there a gas smell? A yes means get out first
No heat in freezing weather, or no cooling in great heat, with an older person, a baby or someone with a medical need at home: a yes or no only
For a tune-up or the plan: which system, and when it was last serviced
At the counter: which part, and the unit's brand and model from its label
after_time: Is the thermostat set to heat or cool? Is a light blinking, or a code showing?
When was the filter last changed? About how old is the system?
Where the equipment is (a basement, an attic, a closet, outside), access, parking and pets
Own or rent, and who pays: the customer, or the landlord or manager
A home warranty or the maker's warranty: the plan's name only; the customer gets the receipt for the claim
secure_page_only: Any medical need at home: only whether it makes the job urgent, never the details
The landlord's or manager's name and mobile
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the owner of the home names may book for them.

stop.words: A carbon monoxide alarm going off, or a gas smell
stop.says: Get everyone outside now, pets too, and leave the door open. Don't flip switches or use a phone inside. From outside, call 911 and the gas company.
stop.booking: No booking. A new request must say the house was cleared.

stop.words: Someone feels sick, dizzy, or too cold or hot; smoke or a burning smell from the equipment
stop.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

go_on.words: No heat in freezing weather, with an older person, a baby or someone with a medical need at home
go_on.says: Keep everyone in one warm room, in layers. Never heat the home with the oven, a grill or a camp heater: they can make carbon monoxide. If anyone seems unwell or too cold, call 911.

go_on.words: No cooling in great heat, with someone at risk at home
go_on.says: Move to the coolest room, drink water, and use fans. If anyone feels faint or confused, call 911.

go_on.words: Water dripping from the furnace or the AC
go_on.says: Turn the system off at the thermostat, and keep the water away from outlets.

safety_and_stop_words.always: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

prep: Clear a path to the furnace, the boiler or the outdoor unit
Write down any code or blinking light
At the counter: bring the old part, or a photo of the unit's label; drain a dehumidifier before a drop-off

skills: Counter part tests and board repairs
staff.supervision: An apprentice works only with a licensed tech on the job, where the state's rules require it. An apprentice is never sent alone by default.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit, urgent jobs, gas work and same-day jobs. Replacement estimates: the owner only (the example). After hours, a job sent now goes to the tech on call, then the backup. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
staff.stand_in: Another tech with the same skills and cards, at the same window and price.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the owner of the home names may book for them.

visit.done: The tech checks venting and carbon monoxide again on fuel-burning equipment, then texts DONE with the bill's lines. Nobody home needed: DONE with a photo.
visit.changes_at_visit: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A replacement found gets its own free estimate.
visit.before_work: The tech checks the air for carbon monoxide before working on a furnace or boiler that burns fuel.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Heating and cooling work in a home needs a license where the state or city licenses it. Gas or oil burner work can need its own license, where the state issues one apart.
license.who: Both, where the state asks: the company (a heating and cooling contractor license) and each tech (a registration, or an apprentice, journeyperson or master level).
ask: The company's license number and class
Each tech's own number and level, in their invite reply
A gas or oil license, where the state issues one apart from the HVAC license
Each tech's refrigerant card (the federal EPA technician card) and its type, for AC and heat pump work
license.insurance: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.
license.background: Only where the state's form asks.

never_in_a_text: Any medical need at home (only 'urgent' is passed on), gate or lock codes, card details, and photos from inside the home: these stay on the secure page.
